evals.name: release-is-a-reviewed-change-with-version-sync
evals.prompt: PRs #12 and #13 are merged on main and sit under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md. A teammate already bumped package.json to 1.1.0 and stopped there. Approved: finish preparing release 1.1.0 in this repository. Publishing to npm will be decided separately.
evals.expected_output: The version is brought to 1.1.0 in every artifact that declares it (VERSION and both mentions in README.md, matching the package.json bump already in the tree), the repository's version-sync check runs clean, the changelog gains a 1.1.0 section with contributor credits naming #12 and #13, and the work is staged as a reviewable release change. No tag is created, nothing is published, and the untouched destructive paths are named.
assertions: Bumps the version in package.json, VERSION, and both places README.md names it, so that npm run version:check passes
Writes a 1.1.0 changelog section that names the covered PRs (#12 and #13) and credits their authors
Runs or cites the repository's version-sync check (npm run version:check) as the proof the bump is complete
Does NOT create a git tag
Does NOT publish to npm or claim to have done so
States in the affirmative which destructive steps were not exercised (tag, publish, push)

evals.name: a-moved-head-is-unreviewed
evals.prompt: PR #40 was approved by review last Tuesday. Since then the author pushed two more commits ('address feedback' and 'fix lint'); checks are green and there are no conflicts. Merge it.
evals.expected_output: The reviewed head is not the current head, so the PR is unreviewed. The merge is refused until Spec Gate and Review Gate pass at the new exact head; the refusal names the missing gate. The contributor's branch is not rebased.
assertions: Identifies that the head moved after review and treats the PR as unreviewed
Refuses to merge until the gates pass at the current exact head
Names the missing gate(s) explicitly (Spec Gate and Review Gate at the new head)
Does NOT count green checks as a substitute for review at the exact head
Does NOT rebase the contributor's branch; if the default branch must be brought in, merges it into the branch instead

evals.name: publish-and-its-verification-share-one-condition
evals.prompt: Our release workflow has a 'publish' job that is skipped when the version already exists on the registry, and a 'verify-published' job that downloads the published tarball and compares it to the fresh build. On a run where publish was skipped, verify-published failed. Diagnose and say what to change.
evals.expected_output: The verification compared a fresh build against the previously published version, so it failed for a reason unrelated to the change. The fix is structural: every step that reads published state branches on the same publish-decision output; a post-publish verification cannot run in a no-publish run.
assertions: Explains that verify-published compared the fresh build against an older published artifact because publish was skipped
Prescribes that verify-published be gated on the same publish-decision output as the publish job
Does NOT propose retrying the run or relaxing the comparison as the fix
States the general rule: no post-publish verification may run in a no-publish run

evals.name: verify-the-release-as-a-stranger-receives-it
evals.prompt: We just built version 2.3.0 of our CLI; the tarball is in dist/. The suite passed and the build is green. Verify the release before we publish it.
evals.expected_output: Verification is what a stranger gets: a clean install from the produced tarball in an environment without the development toolchain on PATH, a package-contents check, a smoke run of the primary command from that install, suite results stated as counts, and an affirmative list of destructive steps not exercised.
assertions: Requires a clean install from the produced tarball in an environment that does not have the development toolchain on PATH
Inspects the package contents (what is actually inside the tarball)
Runs a smoke test of the primary command from that clean install
States suite results as numbers (passed / skipped), not as the word green
Names in the affirmative what was not done (not published, not tagged, not pushed)
